title: Core Windows Auth model / AD / Kerberos / NTLM
meaning: Windows Authentication uses the user's Windows/domain identity instead of app-managed username/password login.
The usual enterprise model is domain-joined clients and servers with Active Directory as the identity authority.
Kerberos is the preferred protocol in domain scenarios; NTLM is fallback/legacy and has different security/delegation behavior.
The browser/server negotiate credentials at the HTTP layer before the app receives an authenticated principal.
Windows Auth is strongest for intranet/corporate environments and usually inappropriate as a public internet login story.
boundary_notes: Basic ASP.NET Core/IIS implementation is in R02.
Dual-scheme cookie/client auth is reserved for R03.
